deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics: no formulas, no derivation and no computation. It is a pencil prose draft in German Kurrent, headed 'p.2.' The archive marks read 'Riemann 10' and folio '41'. It belongs to the bundle 'R.Ohr', so it is almost certainly a draft of the methodological introduction to Riemann's fragment 'Mechanik des Ohres', published posthumously by Henle in 1867. The previous page holds measurement notes in mm with small sketches, plausibly dimensions of ear structures. The next page is a draft letter.

The argument, as far as it can be read: 'One is therefore compelled to a [struck word] {inserted: grounding/explanation of the} phenomena [or a reversed procedure], in which the given effect (Wirkung) is taken as given/necessary, and the causes [are sought] ... For the moving [mechanism?] the procedure so successful in physics(?) is lacking: to bring about the conditions oneself (i.e. to vary them experimentally), and [to produce/examine] each one by itself ...'

This matches the known methodological position of 'Mechanik des Ohres'. Physics can vary the conditions of a phenomenon at will. The physiology of a sense organ cannot do this. So one must reason backwards from the organ's known performance (the effect) to the mechanism that must produce it.

There is nothing mathematical to restate or complete.
errors: No mathematical content, so there are no mathematical errors to report. The machine transcription is very unreliable in several words; see the corrections.

results.what: Methodological remark for the physiology of the ear. Because the conditions cannot be varied experimentally as in physics, one must infer the mechanism (causes) from the given performance of the organ (effect).
results.modern_name: Inverse or 'teleological-mechanical' method in sensory physiology; analysis by inference from function
results.usually_credited_to: Bernhard Riemann, 'Mechanik des Ohres' (posthumous, Henle & Pfeufer's Zeitschrift f. rat. Medicin, 1867)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a prose draft of the introduction to Riemann's known, published ear-mechanics fragment. It contains no mathematics and no new result.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the inserted text above the line plausibly reads 'Begründung der' as given. The struck word before it is illegible. 'Erscheinungen' is plausible.

Line 2: the opening word is unclear ('Vorhersagen' is doubtful). 'genöthigt, wobei die gegebene Wirkung als ...' seems right. The word read as 'unumgänglich' may instead be 'unvermeidlich' or a similar word; uncertain.

Line 3: begins with a struck word, then 'Bewegende' (?). The phrase is more plausibly '... fehlt das in der Physik so erfolgreiche Verfahren' than 'in der Physiologie'; this fits the published methodological argument but is uncertain. It continues 'die Bedingungen'.

Line 4: 'selbst zu verschaffen' may be 'selbst herzustellen' or 'zu verändern'. The repeated 'und jede ... selbst und jede' is probably 'und jede einzeln für sich ...'. The last word, read as 'Erfahrungen', is doubtful.
The vertical rule and dash at left and the marks 'Riemann 10' and '41' are archival or structural, not text.
